.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
No changes to the forecast.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- 1) Benign weather continues through the remainder of October
  with near to above normal temperatures expected. 
 
- 2) On-off rain showers are possible beginning Sunday into
  early next week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...Benign weather continues through the remainder 
of October with near to above normal temperatures expected. 

A weak front to our south will retreat northward as a warm front
Wednesday morning. A large area of high pressure will build to 
the north Thursday through Saturday. As a result, expect passing
high clouds and a series of wind shifts with each of the 
frontal passages. Winds will change to the south and southwest 
late Wednesday through Friday. This will yield seasonable to 
above normal temperatures for the remainder of the workweek. 
Highs will generally range from the mid 60s and low 70s though 
Wednesday with low to mid 70s Thursday and mid to upper 70s 
Friday. This is in part to the position of the high to the 
north leading to increased southeast to southwest winds across 
the region. Overnight lows will remain mild as well in the mid 
40s and low 50s.

There is the potential for some low clouds, fog, or even a
little drizzle during the late night into morning hours each of
the next few days as onshore flow develops.


KEY MESSAGE 2...On-off rain showers are possible beginning Sunday
into early next week.

Surface high pressure lingers on Friday before tracking north of the 
region on Saturday, with generally sunny & warm conditions 
persisting through then. Highs on Friday could reach into the mid-to-
upper 70s across the metros as this persistent high pressure has 
allowed for temperatures to gradually build throughout the week.

Meanwhile, a broad area of low pressure will form over the Midwest 
and then track east late in the weekend, bringing increasing cloud 
cover to the region throughout the day Saturday. A stemming cold 
front will cause temperatures to drop Saturday as this 
system tracks through the Mid-Atlantic, with potential rain showers 
beginning on Sunday. Uncertainty remains high on total spread and 
rainfall accumulation as the system looks somewhat disorganized in 
model guidance. Regardless, this will be the first chance for rain 
in well over a week across the region. While temperatures drop back 
into the upper 60s Saturday & Sunday, this remains somewhat above 
average for the start of November. 

As this system tracks offshore by Tuesday, a second, potentially 
more potent upper-level low could form over the Plains and make its 
way to the region by the middle of next week. Uncertainty remains 
high regarding the track of this system, but this could bring 
additional rainfall to the region as we get into November.

&&

.AVIATION /19Z TUESDAY THROUGH SUNDAY/...
VFR conditions are expected through tonight. Winds will remain 
light out of the north to northeast. Light onshore flow could 
lead to some patchy low clouds/fog in outlying areas late 
tonight.

Winds will shift to the southeast Wednesday ahead of a warm 
frontal boundary. This will lead to the potential for low 
clouds and fog, especially at CHO and MRB given the marine 
influence/increased surface moisture banking along the eastern 
side of the Blue Ridge mountains and up the Potomac River Valley.
Confidence in this is low, although hi-res models have shown 
some consistency in recent cycles. Aside from early morning low
clouds and/or fog, VFR conditions are expected Wednesday night 
through Friday as high pressure builds along the coast. Winds 
will turn south to southwesterly Thursday.

VFR conditions are anticipated to persist through Saturday. 
Beginning Sunday, a passing cold front could bring rain showers and 
lowering cloud decks that could bring temporary sub-VFR conditions 
to terminals. Winds generally stay under 10 knots, flowing 
northwesterly Saturday before shifting southeasterly on Sunday in 
the wake of the front. 

&&

.MARINE...
Light northeast to east winds expected through tonight. Winds 
become southeasterly Wednesday before turning southerly Thursday.
Some channeling is possible at times, though overall gradients 
look weak. Winds stay below SCA thresholds through the end of 
the month. 

Winds remain below SCA thresholds through the weekend. Southerly 
winds shift northwesterly on Friday, then southeasterly by Sunday in 
the wake of a cold front.

&&

.TIDES/COASTAL FLOODING...
Light onshore flow Wednesday into Thursday may push sensitive 
shoreline close to minor flood stage. Areas most at risk for
reaching minor tidal flood thresholds would be places like 
Annapolis and Alexandria mainly during the evening tide cycles 
(which are astronomically higher).
